dossier.public_summary: The 292 ppm, 0.9 Earth-radius transit is flat-bottomed with 65 events and flat odd/even and no secondary, and centroid imaging puts the source on the target with no neighbour within 1 pixel able to mimic it. The star is a spotted 4950 K K dwarf with large variability and bad astrometry (RUWE 26.31), which explains the 1.1-day-like variation and long duration, but a nearby eclipsing binary or blended dip is ruled out. It is the best explanation as a small planet pending radial-velocity mass confirmation.

reasons.why: Nearly Earth-size (rp/rstar 0.0171, undiluted depth 292.4 ppm) - planet-sized, far below stellar regime; flat-bottomed shape v_sigma -1.084 with fit_b 0.196 supports transit

Difference imaging in 2 sectors gives offset 3.354 arcsec err 3.939 arcsec sigma 0.8515; suspects at 52.9, 57.6, 72.0 arcsec ruled out 12.6, 13.8, 17.5 sigma; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0 positively favors on-target
Odd 274.9 ppm vs even 260.8 ppm depth_ratio 1.1 with diff 14.09 ppm, no odd/even difference, arguing against binary at 2x period
No secondary (depth 3.984 ppm snr 0.216, depth_over_dip 0.01403, best_brightening_snr 10.29) and sectors.p_constant 0.8355 steady depth 291.8 ppm, 248 ppm, 270 ppm; 65 transits share 0.08355

Rotation tool found 7.737 d in sector 56 (4715 ppm amplitude) and 9.101 d in sector 82, inconsistent with signal 1.11 d; this 1.10 d variability appears in sector 83 (1822 ppm, false_alarm 2.9488697038048805e-165) but coexists with phase_curve amplitude 339.3 ppm chi2 298.6 that is common for active K dwarf (RUWE 26.31, VARIABLE) and does not produce V shape; rule says rotation counts only with large swing or non-transit shape - here shape is flat
Duration 1.54 central_h 0.9679, b 0.196 fit_log_density_ratio -2.183 is for star density inconsistency only; no a priori radius argues against it and size remains <1 Rearth. RV fields missing

reasons.value: RUWE 26.31, star_density_penalty 305.6 excess_noise_sig 12130 indicate binary/on-target systematics and explain phase_curve; xgboost planet_rank 0.14 is low for same reason, but centroid, flat bottom and planet size positively favour planet over blend/EB with no secondary
